correctness.rationale: For generic central plane the number of crossed edges is its section vertex count; exactly 36 minimal-distance edges. The exact 12 vertex-normal great circles have 132 pair crossings and no triple intersections, so Euler gives 134 chambers. Exact arithmetic enumerates 134 distinct face-sign vectors, all signed corner cosines, and the six disjoint count/area classes. Girard gives the four closed probability formulas; their total and expectation satisfy independent identities. The bundled exact verifier executed successfully, and an independently coded 500,000-sample edge-crossing experiment matches within 0.00046. No infinite extrapolation from finite simulation is used.

value.rationale: The regular truncated cube is a canonical 24-vertex Archimedean solid with four nonzero central-section polygon types. Resolving the exact six spherical region classes gives a complete natural type distribution, with the modest but genuine 6.73% decagonal probability and nontrivial 15.11% quadrilateral probability. The exact law is more informative than a moment or general computability recipe; the 134-cell classification supplies re-usable geometric structure for comparisons with other Archimedean solids.
